label: first copy step (input = orig token 0, outputting token 1) in long sequences containing r/x
explanation: Fires only at the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx == 1, input is the fed-back first original token, output is original token 1): 99.7% of activations and 99.9% of mass are there. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases and essentially never at later copy steps. Firing rate and magnitude rise steeply with sequence length (L=9 has 62% of mass, L=8 26%, L<=6 about 2%). Within those steps it is gated by sequence content: much more likely and stronger when the original sequence contains r or x (next_out = r has 9.9x lift), and the top activations have several r tokens early in the sequence. Identity of the input token has only weak effect (q/u slightly favored). The simple predicate gets about 0.8 of mass but precision is low (~0.29), since many long sequences with r/x at this step stay inactive; the exact content condition was not captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig3=r (+5.05), prev_tok=<DEL> (+4.97), recall_idx=1 (+4.97), orig2=r (+4.69), orig4=r (+4.29), orig3=x (+3.11). Lower it: in_tok=r (-4.81), in_first=1 (-4.28), orig3=q (-3.35), orig8=- (-3.13).
